stem: Harry is a 2-year-old boy presenting with a barking cough, inspiratory stridor at rest, mild coryzal symptoms, moderate respiratory distress, and normal immunisations. Which one of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
explanation: This presentation is classic for croup (viral laryngotracheobronchitis): barking cough, inspiratory stridor, preceding coryzal symptoms, and an otherwise well child. The normal immunisation status and gradual upper respiratory prodrome make epiglottitis and bacterial tracheitis less likely.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: Preserve existing options; the stem most strongly supports croup.

optionExplanations.A: Usually presents with high fever and toxic appearance, often with a more severe and rapidly progressive illness.
optionExplanations.B: Classic presentation: barking cough, inspiratory stridor, and preceding viral symptoms in a young child.
optionExplanations.C: Would usually have features of allergic reaction such as urticaria, facial swelling, wheeze, or hypotension.
optionExplanations.D: Typically causes drooling, dysphagia, muffled voice, and a toxic appearance; less likely in an immunised child.
optionExplanations.E: Would more often have sudden onset symptoms and a choking episode rather than a viral prodrome.

Clinical scenario 3 - Harry

Harry, a two year old boy, presents with a barking cough and stridor at rest. He had been well up until this evening, apart from a mild runny nose and slight cough. On examination he has moderate respiratory distress with intercostal and subcostal recessions and tug. His RR is 35, HR 140 and saturations 94% in room air. He has a clear chest and inspiratory stridor at rest. He has been previously well and his immunisations are up to date.

The following five questions refer to Harry's clinical scenario.
